newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's big brewers expected to show mixed results.
newsitem.headline: Japan's big brewers expected to show mixed results.

text.p: Japan's big beer makers are expected to show mixed results when they unveil their earnings for calendar 1996 on Thursday, analysts say.
Kirin Brewery Co Ltd's sales and parent current profits are seen falling sharply due to sluggish sales of its mainstay brands -- Ichibanshibori and Lager.
Asahi Breweries Ltd is expected to post a rise in sales and profits helped by robust sales of its flagship Super Dry beer.
Third-ranked Sapporo Breweries Ltd is also expected to see its sales and profits rise.

Analysts said Kirin"s parent current profit in 1996 would likely be around 50 billion yen ($403 million) on sales of 1.3 trillion yen ($10.4 billion), down from 75.3 billion yen ($607 million) on sales of 1.38 trillion yen ($11.1 billion) in 1995.

Asahi, in contrast, is expected to post a parent current profit of about 25 billion yen ($201 million), up from 21.7 billion yen ($175 million) a year earlier. Sapporo"s profit is seen rising to 14.5 billion yen ($116 million), compared with 14.3 billion yen ($115 million) in 1995.
"Kirin"s sluggish sales were largely due to a mistake in its marketing strategy," said Masaaki Yamaguchi, an analyst at Nomura Research Institute.

He said Kirin had redirected its marketing efforts towards mass retailers at the expense of its traditional base of local liquor shops, but the move allowed its arch-rival Asahi to chip away at Kirin"s share of sales by small retailers.
Asahi claims to have captured the largest share of the domestic beer market in January. It had 38.3 percent of the market while Kirin had 37.2 percent, an Asahi spokesman said.
Sapporo's share was 19.0 percent while unlisted Suntory Ltd trailed with 5.6 percent, he said.
Asahi"s rise to the top was largely due to a sharp year-on-year increase in sales of its Super Dry beer, he said.
Analysts expect competition in the beer market to keep bubbling as the top four battle for market share amid flat demand.
Japan"s beer market has matured and has little room for further growth, said Akihiro Shimoda, an analyst at Nikko Research Center.
He said the market's growth rate in 1997 is expected to be unchanged at about one percent. ($1=124 yen)
